limitations: The theorem applies only to alphabet {0,1}, word length five, and incoming radius three.
The computed classification is finite and does not establish an all-parameter formula.
Literature comparison does not independently certify worldwide historical priority.

scientific_integrity.asserted_domain: Directed binary de Bruijn graph on five-letter words; radius-three closed incoming balls.
scientific_integrity.claim: Minimum identifying-code size sixteen; exactly four labeled optimal codes, given explicitly; three classes under global bit interchange.
scientific_integrity.computation_evidence: Independent prefix-based and reverse-BFS implementations; exhaustive enumeration of 65536 one-per-prefix selections in each.
scientific_integrity.proof_evidence: Disjoint-prefix lower bound, sixteen exact symmetric-difference constraints that force fourteen codewords, and complete signatures for four remaining cases.
scientific_integrity.proved_limits: No general statement for larger orders, radii, alphabets, or undirected graphs.

title: Four sharp radius-three identifying codes on the binary five-word de Bruijn digraph
